SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSINTRODUCTION

What should survive a completed task?

Illustrative example · an agent reconciles a financial report, then receives a new company’s files.

Keep a reusable procedure

Check units and reporting periods.
Reconcile totals before writing.
Record when those checks apply.

Test it on later work

New company: does the procedure help?
Different task: should it be retrieved?
Later updates: does it still work?

Self-evolution here means experience changes retained state that shapes later behavior.

SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSINTRODUCTION

Learning over time and learning to adapt are different questions

Two established ideas apply to the complete agent, including its external state.

Continual learning

Learn from successive tasks.
Balance adaptation with retention.

Forward transfer: help on new tasks.
Backward transfer: change on old tasks.

Meta-learning

Use experience to improve adaptation.

Learn a starting point, update data,
or a method for proposing changes.
Editable code is one route.

Deployment learning updates the running system; offline optimization may produce a fixed agent.

SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSINTRODUCTION

What is retained—and what does it help the system do?

Memory, code, and weights can each support task behavior or future adaptation.

Where the change livesExamples of retained stateWhat it can support
Memory / agent skillsFacts, lessons, instructions, scriptsTask execution; future proposals
Prompts / harness codeInstructions and tool orchestrationTask execution; update generation
Model weightsLearned representations or policiesTask answers; update-data generation

These mechanisms overlap. A learned improvement method can live in code or in weights.

SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSCONCLUSION

Experience can pay when useful expertise is reused

Conditional synthesis of the evidence · not a measured break-even rule

01

Add missing expertise

WikiSkill improves held-out tasks. FinEvo narrows the gain with expert skills.

Compare strong starting guidance
02

Use it where it fits

AgentStream exposes method-dependent gains. SEAL shows why retention needs its own test.

Select relevant state; revisit old tasks
03

Repay the learning effort

Update design and extra attempts change the alternatives. Reuse can spread development cost.

Count development + operation

Learned adaptation can expand this opportunity. Sustained economical compounding remains unestablished.

SELF-EVOLVING AGENTSCONCLUSION

Test reuse, retention, and cost on the same task stream

Proposed evaluation · commit to the test before optimizing the system

QuestionMeasureLimitation it can reveal
Does it add value?Retain vs reset; expert skill; extra attemptsWhich benefit requires experience?
Where does it transfer?Vary task recurrence and task mixingWhen retained expertise is applicable
What does it preserve?Revisit earlier tasks under fixed toolsForgetfulness versus environment change
Does it repay the effort?Development + operation at stated reuseBenefit relative to lifetime resources

Use independent runs and evaluation. Frozen reuse and resumed adaptation answer different questions.

Appendix · one-shot authoring is a different test

SkillsBench compares agents given curated skill packs, no skills, or one-shot self-authored skills.

Curated skills help on average

Expert procedures are a meaningful baseline for an evolving agent.

Benefits still vary across tasks.

Self-authoring is one-shot here

Three tested configurations underperform no skills.

No repeated outcome-feedback loop: this does not settle iterative learning.

SkillsBench v4: human curation cost and autonomous authoring effort are not matched.

Appendix · editing an agent and editing its improver differ

The important boundary is which learning decisions experience can change.

SystemWhat can changeWhat remains externally specified
SICAAgent implementationExpand the best-scoring agent
DGMAgent code; alternate lineagesImprovement-instruction generator
HyperagentsTask code + improvement codeOuter archive and evaluation

Edit permission makes a hypothesis testable. It does not establish that the edits help.
